title: DWARF debug information format
summary: DWARF is the standard debug information format for ELF (and other) binaries. It provides source-level debugging: line number tables (mapping PC to source line), variable locations (register/stack), type information, and call frame information (CFI) for unwinding. DWARF uses sections: .debug_info (DIEs - Debugging Information Entries), .debug_line (line number program), .debug_str (string table), .debug_abbrev (abbreviation table), .debug_frame/.eh_frame (call frame info).

structure.meaning: DIEs (Debugging Information Entries): tree of tagged entries describing types, variables, functions, scopes.
Tag: DW_TAG_compile_unit, DW_TAG_subprogram, DW_TAG_variable, DW_TAG_base_type, DW_TAG_pointer_type, etc.
Attributes: DW_AT_name, DW_AT_type, DW_AT_location, DW_AT_low_pc, DW_AT_high_pc, DW_AT_decl_file, DW_AT_decl_line, etc.
Line number program: state machine mapping addresses to source lines (file, line, column).
Abbreviation table: templates for DIEs (which attributes each tag has).
Call Frame Information (CFI): unwind rules for each function (how to restore registers and SP).
Little-Endian Base 128: variable-length integer encoding (7 bits per byte, MSB = continue).
DW_OP_reg0 (register), DW_OP_fbreg (frame base + offset), DW_OP_addr (absolute address), DW_OP_deref (dereference).

notes: DWARF is used by GDB, LLDB, and all major debuggers.
CFI (.eh_frame) is used for stack unwinding (backtraces) even in optimized (no frame pointer) code.
DWARF supports inlined functions, templates (C++), and optimized code.
Location lists (DW_AT_location with ranges) handle variables that move during execution.
